core.title: Group DESIRED OUTCOMES into cohesive features by a named grouping strategy
core.given: DESIRED OUTCOMES that belong, or are being placed, in a user-facing feature.
core.when: The planner creates, fills, regroups, or changes the meaning of a feature or its DESIRED OUTCOMES.
core.then: Group the feature's DESIRED OUTCOMES by shared JTBD step, shared measured dimension, shared controlled object, or a coherent user story (any of these strategies, possibly several at once), with at most 10 DESIRED OUTCOMES per group.
prefer: by_step: DESIRED OUTCOMES that share the same JTBD step (<=10).
by_dimension: DESIRED OUTCOMES that measure the same dimension (<=10).
by_object: DESIRED OUTCOMES that control the same object (<=10).
by_coherence: DESIRED OUTCOMES that form a coherent user story (<=10).
Use cues to find a coherent grouping: shared object of control, shared metric kind, shared plane/domain, same user story/flow.
Keep every feature user-facing and cohesive.
avoid: Miscellaneous / catch-all buckets of unrelated DESIRED OUTCOMES.
core.why: Cohesive, user-facing features of bounded size keep acceptance scope reviewable and keep the feature within its size budget; miscellaneous buckets hide unrelated work and break cohesion.
evidence: Each feature's DESIRED OUTCOMES fit at least one grouping strategy (by_step, by_dimension, by_object, or by_coherence); the heuristic cues (object of control, metric kind, plane/domain, user story/flow) may be used to recognise this but are guidance, not an extra required check.
No feature/group contains more than 10 DESIRED OUTCOMES.
No feature is a miscellaneous bucket; each is user-facing.
verification: The central property is semantic and llm_judged: whether a feature's DESIRED OUTCOMES share a JTBD step, a measured dimension, a controlled object, or a coherent user story. A mechanical check can at most verify the group-size count and flag miscellaneous-looking buckets.

Term grouping_strategy = how DESIRED OUTCOMES are grouped into a feature; values: by_step (share the same JTBD step, <=10), by_dimension (measure the same dimension, <=10), by_object (control the same object, <=10), by_coherence (form a coherent user story, <=10). Strategies are alternatives and may overlap; no exclusivity is required.

Term grouping_heuristic = cues for coherent grouping: shared object of control, shared metric kind, shared plane/domain, same user story/flow; avoid: miscellaneous buckets. Cues are advisory aids, not a separate pass condition.
Count threshold: at most 10 DESIRED OUTCOMES per group, inclusive (a group of exactly 10 passes).

Activation needs a planning-phase observer and a diff-level observer that detects feature/DESIRED_OUTCOME membership changes and semantic edits; these are observer requirements, not extra agent obligations.

values: desired outcome added to or removed from feature
desired outcome meaning changed (step, dimension, object or story)

fires: Planner creates a new feature and assigns DESIRED OUTCOMES to it.
Planner moves DESIRED OUTCOMES between features or splits a feature that grew too large.
Planner adds a DESIRED OUTCOME to an existing feature whose other DESIRED OUTCOMES share no step, dimension, object or story with it.
Planner edits a DESIRED OUTCOME or feature so that its JTBD step, measured dimension, controlled object or user story changes, even though feature membership stays the same.
doesNotFire: Wording-only edits to a DESIRED OUTCOME or feature that leave its step, dimension, object and story unchanged.
Coder implementing or testing code for an already-planned feature.
Docs changes that do not touch feature/DESIRED_OUTCOME structure or meaning.

neutralityNotes: This convention governs the planning phase and ATDD plan artifacts (features, DESIRED OUTCOMES); it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so the core reproduces the Bun text essentially verbatim and bunOnly is empty. The only profile dependency is how a stack concretely identifies the feature-plan and DESIRED OUTCOME plan-artifact kinds (roles.plan_artifact.kinds). The neutral schema has no per-fact note field; the observer requirements in the Bun notes are preserved through the facts' observability values and a verification entry. The 'user-facing' half that bun.json proposes to split out (planner.feature.user-facing) is kept in prefer/avoid/evidence exactly as in bun.json, so the core imposes the same single then-obligation with no content lost.
